name: openGym
description: openGym is a self-hosted gym and body-weight tracker. Plan weekly routines, log workouts with supersets and cardio, track body weight, measurements and personal records, and browse a library of more than 5,600 exercises with animations. Every profile keeps its own data and syncs across devices; the web app installs to the home screen, and an Android app can pair with your server. This script builds the web app from source and runs the Node.js API behind nginx.

notes.text: openGym is served over plain HTTP at http://<IP> with password sign-in switched on (PASSWORD_LOGIN=1): choose Create new profile and pick a name and a password. Passkeys, the app's default, cannot work on an IP address, because browsers only offer them on HTTPS under a hostname, so the sign-in screen offers passwords until you switch as described below.

The first profile created becomes the admin (FIRST_USER_ADMIN=1), so create yours right after the install. Anyone who can reach the address can create a profile; to close signup, set INVITE_ONLY=1 (and ALLOW_GUEST=0 to remove guest mode) in /opt/opengym_data/.env after your own profile exists, then run systemctl restart opengym.
Over plain HTTP the password and the session cookie cross the network unencrypted. Keep openGym on a network you trust, or put it behind HTTPS as described below.

ORIGIN in /opt/opengym_data/.env must be exactly the address in the browser bar (http://<IP> as installed). If the container's IP changes or you open openGym under a hostname, set ORIGIN and RP_ID to that address and run systemctl restart opengym; until then sign-ins fail with "cross-origin request refused".

Passkeys: put openGym behind a reverse proxy or tunnel that terminates HTTPS for a real hostname (Caddy, Nginx Proxy Manager, Traefik, Cloudflare Tunnel) and points at http://<IP>:80, set RP_ID=gym.example.com and ORIGIN=https://gym.example.com in /opt/opengym_data/.env, then run systemctl restart opengym. Profiles made with a password keep signing in and can add a passkey under Settings > Account > Passkeys. Settle on the hostname before people register passkeys: changing RP_ID later invalidates every passkey made under the old one.

There is deliberately no self-signed certificate on the IP: an IP address can never be a passkey hostname, and browsers refuse service workers on untrusted certificates, so it would add a certificate warning and enable nothing. Push notifications, Keep screen awake and offline use also need a trusted HTTPS address.
The Android app pairs with the plain http://<IP> address: sign in on the website, then use Settings > Account > Pair the mobile app.

Accounts, workouts, uploaded photos and videos and the key that signs every session live in /opt/opengym_data together with the .env; back up that folder. Updates replace /opt/opengym and leave it untouched.
Install and every update build the web app from source with Node.js 22, which peaks at about 0.9 GB of RAM. The running app needs about 150 MB.
